correctness.rationale: The fixed-point digit support yields the exact 2-adic island-gap ruler. A length-2p square cannot meet three islands; paired ones force two adjacent islands separated by the minimum g. Boundary mismatch forces the square to start precisely at -a with 0<=a<=g; conversely each such factor exists by choosing an internal minimal gap. The unique maximal circular zero run proves primitivity. Replayed Python verification passed 23 base-level cases, and supplies independent finite checks rather than asserting an infinite exhaustive proof.

value.rationale: The result gives a complete exact infinite two-parameter square-root set and multiplicity at natural substitution periods for generalized Cantor words, including a strict and asymptotically explicit fraction of their primitive cyclic rotations that support square factors. It distinguishes two natural factor invariants—occurring conjugacy and adjacent repetition—and provides a new structural gap-localization method. It is neither a finite census nor a routine re-expression of Lie class counts.
